content: Disulfiram should never be administered to a patient who is currently intoxicated with alcohol or without the patient’s explicit knowledge and consent. Patients must avoid taking disulfiram for at least 12 hours after consuming alcohol. It is important to note that a reaction to alcohol may still occur for up to two weeks after discontinuing disulfiram. Disulfiram is prescribed to treat chronic alcoholism. It works by causing unpleasant physical effects when even small amounts of alcohol are consumed. These effects include facial flushing, headache, nausea, vomiting, chest pain, weakness, blurred vision, mental confusion, sweating, choking, difficulty breathing, and anxiety. These symptoms typically begin about 10 minutes after alcohol enters the body and can last for an hour or longer. While disulfiram is not a cure for alcoholism, it serves as a deterrent to drinking. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Disulfiram is available in tablet form and is taken orally, usually once daily. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take disulfiram exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it, or take it more frequently than prescribed. If you have difficulty swallowing the tablets, you may crush them and mix the medication with water, coffee, tea, milk, soft drinks, or fruit juice. Before taking disulfiram, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to disulfiram or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially amitriptyline (Elavil), anticoagulants (such as warfarin), isoniazid, metronidazole (Flagyl), phenytoin (Dilantin), any over-the-counter drugs containing alcohol, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of diabetes, thyroid disease, epilepsy, brain damage, or kidney or liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking disulfiram, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your surgeon or dentist that you are taking disulfiram. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how disulfiram affects you. While taking disulfiram, do not consume any alcoholic beverages, including wine, beer, or medications containing alcohol (such as cough syrups). Avoid alcohol for at least 12 hours before your first dose and for several weeks after stopping the medication. Additionally, avoid foods and beverages containing alcohol, such as sauces and vinegars. If you miss a dose of disulfiram, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Disulfiram may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following minor side effects, especially if they persist or worsen: skin rash, acne, mild headache, drowsiness, fatigue, impotence, or a metallic or garlic-like taste in the mouth. If you experience severe side effects, such as excessive tiredness, weakness, lack of energy, loss of appetite, upset stomach, vomiting, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or dark urine, contact your doctor immediately. Store disulfiram in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor will order specific lab tests to monitor your response to disulfiram. Always carry an identification card stating that you are taking disulfiram and providing emergency contact information for your doctor or healthcare provider. If you need an identification card, ask your pharmacist or doctor how to obtain one. Avoid contact with or inhalation of fumes from products containing alcohol, such as paint, paint thinner, varnish, shellac, aftershave lotions, colognes, and rubbing alcohol. These products, when combined with disulfiram, may cause headache, nausea, localized redness, or itching. Before using an alcohol-containing product, test it by applying a small amount to a small area of your skin for 1–2 hours. If no redness, itching, or adverse effects occur, you may use the product safely. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
